Subject: Control-plane/data-plane canalization: attachment brief & feedback request

Alex / NetBridge team —

Thanks again for carving out time this morning. As discussed, attached are two artifacts to help the next design pass: a draw.io sketch that separates the control-plane "canal" from the data-plane traffic flow and an annotated attachment matrix that lists the cross-connects we expect at your edge POPs. High level goals: 

- Strict separation of control telemetry and model traffic (no data-plane token payloads traversing the control path).
- Minimal NAT boundaries for inference nodes; prefer 1:1 service IPs where possible to simplify observability.
- Explicit handoff for TLS termination at the edge and mTLS for internal services.

Asks: 
1) Can you review the canalization sketch (RBW-controlplane-dataplane-canals-v1.drawio) and confirm whether your edge NAT/ACL constraints allow the proposed direct service IPs?
2) Please validate any carrier cross-connect lead times in the attachment matrix and flag ports we should avoid for SLA reasons.
3) If you have any mandatory egress inspection points (DPI, proxy), point them out so we can annotate fault domains.

Timeline: we want to freeze the attachment matrix by Wed 17 Jul so engineering can order cross-connects.

Thanks — appreciate a quick thumb up or quick notes.

—Rishi

Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-plane/data-plane canalization: attachment brief & feedback request

Rishi —

Thanks for the artifacts. Quick notes from the NetBridge ops side after a first pass: 

- The canalization sketch looks good, we like the explicit split. One operational constraint: two of our central POPs (SFO-3, ORD-1) have shared eBGP fabrics that currently NAT a /27 for service IPs. We can switch to 1:1 service IPs but expect a 7–10 business day coord for provisioning.
- For TLS termination: we can offer TLS passthrough to your edge proxies (so Redwood maintains certs inside the cluster) or terminate at our F5 and re-encrypt to your control plane — both are viable but have different monitoring impacts. We lean toward passthrough for fewer touch points.
- DPI/proxy: we have an inline proxy at ORD-1 used for regulated traffic only. If you intend to route regulated model inputs through ORD-1, we'll need an SOC report and an allowed list.

I'll loop in our infra scheduler to start the cross-connect requests once you confirm final IP counts per POP.

Appreciate the timeline.

—Alex
Alex Gomez
NetBridge Solutions — Cloud Partnerships
alexg@netbridge.com

Rishi / team —

Thanks Alex for the initial constraints. A couple of internal clarifications and edits I propose for the diagram and matrix before we send a final request to NetBridge: 

1) Control-plane east-west telemetry: add a dedicated metrics port (TCP 9100) with ACLs that only allow Redwood observability collectors. This prevents any accidental telemetry egress through customer proxies.
2) Add an optional flow for model-cache warmup traffic that is tagged as best-effort and routed via the low-priority data plane; call it out in the matrix so NetBridge can classify QoS.
3) Where NetBridge says a POP will NAT a /27, we should include an alternative plan B where we colocate a tiny NAT gateway inside our tenant to preserve service IP stability until the cross-connect is provisioned. Note this as a temporary operational lane.

Also: Kimberly, can you validate whether any of the proposed POPs are blocked by our compliance zones (we should not send regulated EU traffic via ORD-1 DPI)?

If no objections, I'll update the draw.io with the metrics port and the warmup flow. Will also add a short note about TLS passthrough vs termination (ops impact) so NetBridge can choose.

—Irene
